relevance.rationale: Proves combinatorial results on triangulations of 3-dimensional pseudo-manifolds improving on Neumann-Zagier, and applies them to give a simplicial formula for the Chern-Simons invariant of an ideally triangulated hyperbolic 3-manifold: V(M) = Vol(M) + i CS(M) as a sum of Rogers dilogarithms over the ideal tetrahedra, with the branch choice per simplex governed by unexpected combinatorics. Theorem 1 gives the formula up to a constant alpha; Theorem 2 shows that integral solutions satisfying a PARITY CONDITION exist and that for those, alpha becomes well-defined modulo an explicit lattice. Both halves are wanted right now. The corpus's fraktur-V = Vol + i CS is built as an explicit analogy to this invariant (notation-register-table7-data, notation-collisions, conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume), its Rogers face is a named object (prop:q-rogers-pentagon-archimedean), and -- most concretely -- computations/one-loop-ambiguity-group.witness.json is an active investigation of exactly a triangulation-dependent ambiguity whose description ends 'which is exactly where the dropped DG flattening monomial lives'. A parity/flattening condition that makes the ambiguity constant well-defined is the shape of the answer that investigation is looking for. references.ts carries neumann-zagier1985 but no entry for this paper.

keyResults.statement: For any solution of the combinatorial system, the complex volume V(M) = Vol(M) + i CS(M) of an ideally triangulated hyperbolic 3-manifold is a sum of Rogers dilogarithms of the tetrahedron parameters, up to a constant alpha depending on the solution.
keyResults.useForFolio: The simplicial formula the corpus's complex-volume analogy is modelled on, and the concrete link between the folio's Rogers face and its hyperbolic-volume face; currently the analogy is stated with only neumann-zagier1985 behind it.

keyResults.locator: Theorem 2 (with the parity condition; Theorem 2.4 / Sects. 4-6)
keyResults.statement: Integral solutions satisfying a parity condition exist, and for such solutions the constant alpha of Theorem 1 is independent of the solution modulo an explicit lattice; dropping the parity condition weakens the conclusion.
keyResults.useForFolio: Directly addresses the corpus's live problem of a triangulation-dependent constant in the one-loop / det J chain. What would need checking before claiming more: whether Neumann's parity condition is the same normalisation as the Dimofte-Garoufalidis flattening monomial the corpus records as dropped, and whether it says anything about the multi-cusp per-cusp factor that borromean_nz_adjoint_torsion.py flags as unpinned at c >= 2. Proposed as compute-check plus remark, NOT aid-proof, because neither of those has been verified.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; this is the source of the simplicial complex-volume formula the corpus's central fraktur-V analogy is built on, and of the parity/ambiguity analysis its live one-loop work needs.

conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume and the notation register both present fraktur-V as the analogue of the Neumann-Zagier complex volume; the simplicial Rogers-dilogarithm formula that makes that object computable comes from here and is uncited.

Check whether the parity condition of Theorem 2 is the normalisation the corpus records as the dropped flattening monomial, by comparing the resulting ambiguity lattice against the unit-group-of-the-trace-field characterisation already recorded in one-loop-ambiguity-group.witness.json. A match would explain the observed ambiguity; a mismatch is equally informative. No external constant may be adopted either way.
